security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU emulates a CSR write to mipreemptcfg (0x348) that sets mfie=0 or sipreemptcfg (0x148) that sets sfie=0, but does NOT also clear the corresponding xie bit (mie in mstatus/sie in sstatus) as a side-effect. Conversely, QEMU allows the TCG interrupt delivery path to signal interrupts when xie=0 but xfie=1 and IPRIO < FITHRESH, without checking the FITHRESH condition — the xie bit is no longer the sole gate for fast interrupts.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: CSR write to mipreemptcfg/sipreemptcfg where mfie/sfie transitions 1→0 must atomically clear mstatus.MIE/sstatus.SIE; conversely, riscv_cpu_do_interrupt must check xfie+FITHRESH as an alternate interrupt-gating path that bypasses xie
security_spec.summary: Smnip fast-interrupt enable (xfie) creates a new interrupt-gating path that bypasses the traditional xie bit when IPRIO < FITHRESH; writing xfie=0 must side-effect-clear xie, and trap entry must save-then-zero xfie to xpfie — failure in any coupling rule silently breaks guest interrupt masking

findings.finding: CSR addresses 0x148 and 0x348 are not defined. The SMNIP ipreemptcfg CSRs do not exist in this QEMU tree, so there is no write path that could violate the mfie/sfie→0 side-effect requirement (clearing MIE/SIE). No privilege-escape vector exists via this mechanism.

/* Gap at 0x148 between CSR_SCOUNTINHIBIT (0x120) and CSR_SISELECT (0x150) */
/* Gap at 0x348 between CSR_MIP (0x344) and CSR_MISELECT (0x350) */

findings.finding: Existing MIE/SIE CSR write handlers manipulate only the standard interrupt-enable bits. No mfie/sfie preemption fields exist in the register layout, so no 1→0 transition side-effect (clearing MIE/SIE) is applicable. The handlers are correct for the currently implemented ISA extensions.

Interrupt delivery path gates on MSTATUS_MIE/MSTATUS_SIE only (lines 2370-2425 for S-mode, lines 2426-2511 for M-mode). There is no alternate xfie+FITHRESH gating path that could bypass the xie check. The TCG interrupt delivery logic is correct for the currently implemented extensions.

Interrupt arbitration uses only MSTATUS_MIE/MSTATUS_SIE as the enable gate (lines 538-549). No FITHRESH threshold comparison exists. The single-gate model is correct for the base ISA and implemented extensions (AIA), with no bypass possible.
